annotatedSteps.description: Finding the roots by equating factors to zero
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
2x + 1 = 0 or x - 3 = 0
x = -1/2 or x = 3
So the roots are -1/2 and 3
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Method carried forward correctly from student's factors (ECF)
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking:
2x - 1 = 0 or x - 3 = 0
x = 1/2 or x = 3
So the roots are 1/2 and 3

results.teacherNote: You split the middle term accurately and correctly solved the resulting factors. Take extra care with signs when taking out common factors: factoring -1 from -x + 3 gives -1(x - 3), yielding x = 1/2 instead of -1/2.

rubric.point: Splitting the middle term correctly (2x² - 6x - x + 3 = 0)
Grouping and factorising into linear factors (2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0
Solving linear factors to find the roots (x = 1/2 or x = 3)

summary: Good presentation and solid understanding of the factorisation method. Be vigilant with negative signs during algebraic grouping to ensure complete accuracy in your final roots.
